title: The articles ang and ng
summary: When to use ang (the main character) and when to use ng (the other characters), and their plurals
goals: Use ang to introduce the subject of a sentence
Use ang in place of ay to stress who did something
Use ng for the receiver of an action, for possession, and for the doer of an -in- verb
Use the plural forms ang mga and ng mga

blocks.t: **Ang** and **ng** are two of the most commonly used words in Tagalog. You met them in Lesson 8, together with **ni**, as words that show possession.

head: Article
Its job
In English
rows: introduces the **main character** in a sentence
introduces the **other, minor characters**, among other things
blocks.title: Ang and ng
A common mix-up
blocks.t: Many learners use **ang** where **ng** should be used, and **ng** where **ang** should be used. The rules below help you tell them apart.

blocks.title: How to say ng
blocks.t: Remember from Lesson 8: **ng** is read like **nang**.
**Ang** introduces a **common noun** that is the **subject** of the sentence. Here it is like the English *the*.

items.tl: Ang batà ay mabaít at masípag.
items.en: The child is good and diligent.
The young woman is eating a mango.

blocks.t: In the second sentence, **ang dalaga** is the subject even though it comes last, and **ng manggà** is the thing being eaten.
b. To stress who the doer is
Putting **ang** where **ay** would go puts the emphasis on the **identity of the doer**: it marks *who* did it.

head: With ay
With ang
rows: Akó ay sumúlat ng kuwénto. (*I wrote a story.*)
Akó **ang** sumúlat ng kuwénto. (*I was the one who wrote the story.*)
Ang batà ay maysakít. (*The child is sick.*)
Ang batà **ang** maysakít. (*The child is the one who is sick.*)
blocks.title: Ay or ang?

items.en: I was the one who wrote the story.
The child is the one who is sick.

blocks.title: The one who…
blocks.t: English does the same job with *the one who*: *I was **the one who** wrote the story.*
a. The receiver of an action

items.tl: Si Elena ay nagluto ng manók.
Ang iná ng báta ay nagpuntá sa paléngke.
items.en: The child's mother went to the market.

items.tl: Ang báhay ng laláki ay bágo.

blocks.t: c. The doer of a passive (-in-) action
Look at the **-in-** verbs from Lesson 15: the doer is introduced by **ng**, and the thing acted upon takes **ang**.

items.tl: Binilí ng batáng babáe ang aklàt.

blocks.title: Ng has three jobs
items: the **receiver** of an action: Bumili **ng** pagkain…
the **doer** of an -in- action: Kináin **ng** áso…

sections.title: Plural forms: ang mga and ng mga

blocks.t: Tagalog follows the **plurality rule** from Lesson 4: plural words must be introduced by the **plural forms** of the articles.

items.tl: Ang mga báhay ng magkákapatid na babáe ay malalakì.
Bumilí ng mga prutas ang lóla.

blocks.title: Magkákapatid
blocks.t: **Magkákapatid** means two or more siblings. With **na babáe** it becomes *sisters*.

blocks.title: Remember
items: **Ang** in place of ay stresses who the doer is: Akó ang sumúlat ng kuwénto.
**Ng** introduces the receiver of an action, an owner, or the doer of an -in- verb.

vocab.note: The book says ng may be translated using the English preposition of or the indefinite articles a and an

exercises.q: Which article is like the English "the" and introduces the main character?
exercises.explain: Ang introduces the subject.

exercises.q: Which article can be translated "of", "a" or "an"?
exercises.explain: Ng introduces the other, minor characters.

exercises.q: Fill in: Kumakain ng manggà ___ dalaga.
exercises.explain: The young woman is the subject: ang dalaga.

exercises.q: Fill in: Bumili ___ pagkain ang babáe.
exercises.explain: Pagkain (food) receives the action, so it takes ng.

exercises.q: Fill in: Kináin ___ áso ang tinápay.
exercises.explain: The doer of an -in- verb takes ng.

exercises.q: Fill in: Ang báhay ___ laláki ay bágo.
exercises.explain: Ng shows possession: the man's house.

options: I was the one who wrote the story.
exercises.answer: I was the one who wrote the story.
exercises.explain: Ang in place of ay stresses who the doer is.

options: The child is the one who is sick.
exercises.explain: With ay it is a plain statement.

exercises.q: Which sentence stresses that it is the child who is sick?
exercises.explain: Ang in place of ay marks the identity of the one who is sick.

exercises.q: In "Kináin ng áso ang tinápay", what does ng show?
exercises.explain: With an -in- verb, ng introduces the doer: the dog.

exercises.q: In "Si Elena ay nagluto ng manók", what does ng show?
exercises.explain: The chicken receives the action of cooking.

exercises.q: What is the plural of ng?
exercises.explain: Ng becomes ng mga.

exercises.q: Fill in: Bumilí ___ prutas ang lóla. (The grandmother bought fruits.)
exercises.explain: Fruits are plural and receive the action: ng mga prutas.

exercises.q: Fill in: ___ báhay ___ áking kaibígan ay nasa Quezon City.
exercises.explain: Ang introduces the subject; ng shows whose house it is.

exercises.q: Fill in: ___ pangálan ___ áking asáwa ay John.
exercises.explain: Ang for the subject, ng for possession.

exercises.q: Fill in: Kumákain ___ gúlay ___ malusóg na batà.
exercises.explain: The vegetables receive the action (ng); the healthy child is the subject (ang).

exercises.q: Fill in: ___ pangálan ___ kapatíd ko ay Peter at Mary.
exercises.explain: Two names, so the plural forms are needed.
Lóla = grandmother.
Kápitbahay = neighbor.
Maysakít = sick.

exercises.en: The child is good and diligent.
exercises.tl: Ang batà ay mabaít at masípag.

exercises.en: The young woman is eating a mango.
I was the one who wrote the story.

exercises.tl: Ang báhay ng laláki ay bágo.
Bumilí ng mga prutas ang lóla.

exercises.q: Match each word to its meaning.
Match each use to its article.

recap: Ang introduces the main character (the subject), like the English the.
Ang in place of ay stresses who the doer is: Akó ang sumúlat ng kuwénto.
Ng introduces the receiver of an action, an owner, and the doer of an -in- verb.
Ng can be translated of, a or an.
Plural: ang mga and ng mga.
